title: Supreme Court Demands Answers on 34 Unnatural Deaths in Manipur Relief Camps
excerpt: A bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant ordered Manipur's chief secretary to file an affidavit explaining why post-mortems were conducted in only 20 cases and why bereaved families received as little as Rs 20,000 in compensation.
body:
• The Supreme Court on Thursday directed Manipur's chief secretary to file an affidavit explaining the deaths — especially unnatural deaths — of internally displaced persons living in relief camps.
  • The directions followed a Justice Gita Mittal committee report recording 34 cases of unnatural death in the camps, of which only 25 were registered as FIRs and post-mortems were conducted in just 20.
  • The bench questioned why families of those who died received only Rs 20,000 to Rs 30,000 in compensation, and ordered the state's legal services authority to ensure an FIR in every case of unnatural death.
  • A report placed before the court referred to 640 deaths in relief camps across eight districts; the next hearing is on October 5, 2026.

The Court's Questions

Expressing shock over the deaths, a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana asked why the state had taken no significant steps on information furnished by the Justice Gita Mittal committee about deaths — including unnatural ones — of internally displaced persons (IDPs) in relief camps.

https://x.com/barandbench/status/2100497219908784238

"We direct the chief secretary of Manipur to file an affidavit on deaths, especially unnatural deaths, at relief camps in Manipur," the bench said in its order, according to PTI. The court also asked the state's top bureaucrat to explain why post-mortems were conducted in only 20 of the 34 reported cases, and why compensation of merely Rs 20,000 to Rs 30,000 had been paid to the families of IDPs who died unnatural deaths while sheltered in the camps.

"Tell your Chief Secretary not to invite orders. Tell us what measures you have taken."

— Chief Justice Surya Kant, during the hearing

The bench further directed the Manipur State Legal Services Authority (MSLSA) to file a separate status report, ensure that FIRs are registered in all cases of unnatural death, ascertain the cause of death in each case, and see that investigations already underway are completed expeditiously. The court stressed that authorities must ensure the safety and dignity of people continuing to live in the camps, and directed that adequate medical facilities and day-to-day necessities be provided to them.

The Mittal Committee's Findings

The court's directions came while hearing a batch of petitions concerning the investigation and trial of sexual violence cases arising from the 2023 ethnic violence in Manipur. The bench took note of the 47th report of the committee headed by former Jammu and Kashmir High Court Chief Justice Gita Mittal, which flagged the deaths in the relief camps and raised questions about compensation.

According to the committee, of 34 cases of unnatural death among displaced persons in the camps, FIRs were registered in only 25, and post-mortems conducted in just 20. The committee had sought more information from the Manipur chief secretary as far back as July 4, but no adequate response was furnished, the court noted. A separate report placed before the apex court referred to 640 deaths in relief camps across eight districts, with post-mortem examinations conducted in only a fraction of cases. The court also took note of a report concerning an alleged sexual assault incident in the camps.

The Wider Manipur Cases

During the hearing, the court also reviewed the progress of investigations into the 2023 violence. Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the CBI and the Manipur government, informed the court that the CBI had investigated 31 cases so far and submitted final reports in 28 of them, with three cases still under investigation.

The bench reiterated the need for special courts to hear the Manipur cases, underlining the pressure on the judicial system from the sheer volume of cases. The matter will next be heard on October 5, 2026.

Diaspora Angle

For the Indian diaspora — including human-rights advocates and community groups that have followed Manipur closely since 2023 — the court's intervention is a reminder that accountability for the displaced extends beyond the headlines of the violence itself to the conditions in which survivors are living and dying more than three years later.

What's Next

All eyes are now on the affidavit the chief secretary must file: it will have to account for each of the 34 unnatural deaths, the missing post-mortems, and the compensation paid. The MSLSA's separate status report on FIRs and investigations will show whether the court's direction for an FIR in every unnatural-death case is being carried out on the ground. The October 5 hearing will test whether the state's response satisfies the bench — or invites the sharper orders the Chief Justice warned about.
